author: manmohanbrahma
about: Every upstream thread Open Inference Fabric opened or joined. Add a thread here when it is filed; scripts/upstream_status.py refreshes status.json daily and lists threads it finds that are not here yet. ref = the item in docs/UPSTREAM.md of the oif repository.

threads.summary: AMD backend for fractiond: a hard VRAM cap per pod with the Linux dmem cgroup. Lab: no measurable cost against the whole GPU; the cap refuses an over-ask.

ours.note: Announces PR #175, reworked to the existing annotation contract; asks about the annotation prefix and the KAI side (KAI#2556)

threads.summary: feat(fractiond): limit AMD GPU memory with the dmem cgroup. --gpu-vendor=amd turns the existing gpu-memory annotations into dmem.max and dmem.min on the container through NRI; AMD guide in docs/amd (refs #173).

ours.note: Answers the maintainer review point by point: re-apply caps on Synchronize, drop dmem.min, dmem.capacity check, runc >= 1.2.0, kernel 6.15; asks where AMD metrics should go
Review fixes pushed (261f6ce, 584b4b8), with a reply on each of the 13 inline comments; lab check of the re-apply path to follow

Lab result on the W7900 node, 11/11: readiness, 4096 MiB dmem.max on create, no dmem.min, re-apply in place after fractiond was down, fail-closed with the clear error; suggests AMD metrics as a follow-up PR

threads.summary: GPU fractions on AMD GPU nodes (amd.com/gpu): node helper, scheduler readiness check, binder reservation, resource-reservation without NVML. Design questions first.

ours.note: Lab measurements: soft memory isolation, 23 GiB taken from a 22.5 GiB share
Update: isolation can be hard with the dmem cgroup; links gpu-fractioning#173

The scheduler cannot size GPU-memory fractions on AMD nodes (reads only nvidia.com/gpu.memory); oif's one-function fix reads beta.amd.com/gpu.vram as the pod-group controller does; lab evidence from T-140

threads.summary: The binder changes the configured reservation-pod resources in place on every GPU reservation.
fix(binder): do not modify the configured reservation pod resources (fixes #2554).

ours.note: Ping for review, offering to split the PR or add tests
Review: the GPU resource is now stripped once in NewService (58019b53); changelog fragment linked to #2554

threads.summary: Fraction pods get runtimeClassName nvidia even when they can only run on AMD GPU nodes.

ours.note: A contributor traced it to the admission webhook and offered a fix; suggested skipping the mutation when no reachable node reports nvidia.com/gpu, until #1544 removes the runtime class
Withdrew the webhook node check; a RuntimeClass with the runc handler set by the platform already avoids the mutation, so a docs note may be enough

threads.summary: CDI/NRI-native GPU injection for fraction pods (opened by others): our AMD device injector as a working NRI example.

ours.note: oif-amd-share NRI plugin for AMD fraction pods

threads.summary: Topology: a required level is never satisfied when all of a job's nodes share a domain below it (e.g. a one-node node pool); found on the lab with Run:ai node pools linked to a network topology.
fix(scheduler): honour a required topology level above the job's lowest common domain (fixes #2593); 5-case test, changelog fragment. Same fix as oif KAI patch 0007.

ours.note: Review: the test requires every idle node to be offered, counted as distinct nodes (534b1f8a)

threads.summary: AMD GPU support in open-source Run:ai: asks the maintainers to reconsider the not-planned AMD threads (#3939, #3940, #3946, #4274, PR #3950) as community-maintained support, with OIF owning the tests and an AMD lab run per release; otherwise a stop-gap fork under its own name, kept in step and offered back.

ours.note: Reopen requests on #3939, #3940, #3946, #4274 and PR #3950, linking the discussion

threads.summary: Feature request: AMD GPU metrics from the AMD GPU Operator's Device Metrics Exporter. Run:ai's AMD rules read amd_gpu_* names no current exporter emits and its Prometheus does not watch kube-amd-gpu, so AMD GPUs are missing from GPU totals, memory, utilization and free GPUs. Offers OIF's working mapping as a PR.
AMD GPU fractions with a hard VRAM cap (dmem cgroup): implementation and lab results, and where it touches Run:ai.
cluster-sync: AMD GPUs missing from the node inventory and the Overview GPU total.

ours.note: AMD is not on the Run:ai roadmap (#3939, #3940, #3946, #4274 and PR #3950 closed as not planned); the AMD changes stay as OIF patches

threads.summary: cluster-sync: count AMD GPUs (amd.com/gpu) in the node inventory (fixes #3939).
Show an AMD icon for workloads on ROCm images.
frontend: AMD icon for workloads on ROCm images (fixes #3940).

ours.note: Reply to 'we are reviewing it': the required approved-issue check cannot pass while #3940 is closed, so the PR waits on discussion #5023; offered a rebase when they review

go-operator: report GPU fractions unavailable when the fractioning daemons have no target nodes (fixes #3941).

threads.summary: Feature request: node labels and DRA attributes for scale-up domains (xGMI hive on MI300/MI350 servers, UALink domain on Helios racks) and partition capabilities, MI455X in amdgpu.ids; for topology-aware scheduling (KAI Topology levels). Points to oif's fake AMD Instinct nodes.

Feature request: pods sharing a GPU without their own amd.com/gpu allocation (KAI/Run:ai fractions) get no per-pod metrics; the exporter labels the GPU with the reservation pod. Asks for attribution by the processes using the GPU (KFD, dmem.current) and a pod UID label. Lab evidence on a W7900.

ours.note: Answer to the triage: what the KAI fraction setup is, and an offer to test any build on a W7900
